title: SunSpec device file
description: A SunSpec device described by its models and their point values: what "sunspecctl serve" runs, what "sunspecctl capture" and "sunspecctl template" write, and what the OT Fabric SunSpec Explorer exports. Implemented by the Go package github.com/otfabric/go-sunspec/devicefile. Unknown members are errors. The schema describes the form of a file; whether the models and points exist in the SunSpec model definitions and the values fit their points is checked when the device is built.

unit_id.description: Modbus unit ID the device answers. Default 1. 0 is the Modbus broadcast address and cannot be served.

base_address.description: Register address of the "SunS" marker. Default 40000. Clients find a device at 0, 40000 or 50000 without being told.

models.description: The models of the device in chain order. A model ID may occur more than once. A file without models describes an empty device.

model.description: One model: given by point values ("points" and "groups"), which are encoded with the SunSpec definition of the model, or by its raw data registers ("registers"), not both. A model with neither has every point not implemented.

name.description: The model's name. Written for the reader; ignored when the file is used.

registers.description: The model's data registers: what follows the ID and length registers. For vendor models, which have no definition, and for anything that must be served bit for bit.
A model given by registers has no points and no groups.

group.description: One instance of a group: its points and the instances of its nested groups.

points.description: Point values by SunSpec point name, as in the model definition. A name may occur once. A point that is left out is not implemented. The order of the members has no meaning; written files list the points in the order of the model definition.

groups.description: Nested groups: group name to list of instances. Count points such as NPt or NCrv are filled in from the number of instances.

anyOf.description: An instance with every point not implemented.
A number. A point with a scale factor takes the engineering value: with "A_SF": -1, "A": 18.3 is stored as 183. For an enum or bitfield point, the number as it is.
The text of a string point, the symbol name of an enum point, or an address (ipaddr, ipv6addr, eui48) in its usual notation.
The names of the bits that are set in a bitfield point; an empty list for none.
The raw registers of the point, exactly as many as the point has.
